checks.after: The poor who wholly lack assets and cannot support themselves shall each be granted one ox.
checks.reason: 全無資產，不能自存 restricts the recipients to the wholly destitute unable to support themselves. The replacement restores both conditions and one ox each without imposing a disputed specialization on 牧牛.

checks.after: If any have surplus private labor and gladly take official oxen to reclaim official fields, let them follow the old Wei and Jin rules.
checks.reason: 私有餘力 supplies the surplus-capacity condition, 樂取 the willingness to take official oxen, and 墾官田 reclamation of official fields. The replacement preserves all three and the Wei–Jin precedent without inventing a rental contract.

checks.after: Irrigation ditches and channels benefit public and private interests; let the responsible officials plan and build them, striving to exhaust the advantages of water and land.
checks.reason: 主者 denotes those responsible rather than a specified profession of engineers. 量造 and 務盡水陸之勢 require planning/construction and full use of water-and-land conditions, both restored here.

checks.after: Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of great forbearance.
checks.reason: 禁黜 is the sanction warranted by their offenses, not something applied to crimes themselves. The replacement also preserves Huang’s concession and self-reproach in 孤之無大量 without endorsing the punishment as the reviewer’s judgment.

checks.after: Master Feng is steadfastly upright and deeply embodies the character of a royal minister.
checks.reason: 蹇蹇 explicitly praises steadfast uprightness, and 深得王臣之體 praises ministerial character rather than merely an isolated utterance. 封生 is respectfully rendered Master Feng, with the encomium remaining Huang’s.

checks.after: Huang personally went to the eastern school to examine students; those whose command of the classics was thorough and outstanding were promoted to fill posts as close attendants.
checks.reason: 親臨 identifies Huang’s personal attendance, 經通秀異 the specified classical learning and distinction, and 擢充近侍 promotion into close attendance. The replacement restores these without inventing examination results or identities.

checks.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people's field rent.
checks.reason: 久旱 specifies a prolonged drought, and 百姓田租 specifies the common people’s field rent. In this administrative context 丐 expresses remission; the replacement preserves the stated cause and object.

checks.after: He made the Bohai people into Xingji County, the Hejian people into Ningji County, the Guangping and Wei commandery people into Xingping County, the Donglai and Beihai people into Yuli County, and the Wu people into Wu County, all subordinate to the state of Yan.
checks.reason: The five group-to-county mappings are expressly enumerated in the Chinese and lost in the original summary. The replacement preserves each mapping and 悉隸燕國 without adding a new migration event or administrative relationship.

checks.after: Again measure affairs to establish offices, measure offices to appoint men, so that offices match need and men do not hold empty posts; estimate the amount of annual revenue and determine their salaries accordingly.
checks.reason: 裁而祿之 means apportion or determine remuneration after estimating annual income; a necessary salary reduction is not stated. The replacement preserves the two preceding matching operations and removes only that unsupported direction of adjustment.

checks.after: Those who labor in the fields receive rewards of public commendation and distinction, while idle farmers suffer the penalty of exclusion from standing among their peers.
checks.reason: 旌顯 is public commendation and distinction, not necessarily a material banner. 不齒 is exclusion from recognized social standing rather than simply absence of an official rank. Both contrasts are faithfully restored.

checks.after: Food must be taken from those who plow to feed them; one person consumes the labor of one person, and with tens of thousands living without working, the loss is likewise in the tens of thousands; how can every household be provided for and every person have enough, and government bring about peace!
checks.reason: The preceding unit establishes idle consumers as the referent of 食之. The replacement retains the one-to-one burden, the corresponding aggregate loss in 損亦如之, both members of 家給人足, and the rhetorical challenge about peaceful government.

checks.after: If not, impose punishment and execution on me at once, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
checks.reason: 登 here supplies immediacy. The conditional contrasts with 臣之所言當也 in the preceding unit, so the punishment is requested by Feng Yu for himself, not for Wang Xian and Liu Ming or for the ruler. Execution and the closing public lesson are retained.

additionalCorrections.before: he clothes the cold and feeds the hungry until every household is provided for.
additionalCorrections.after: he clothes the cold and feeds the hungry, so that every household is provided for and every person has enough.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 寒者衣之，饑者食之，使家給人足。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 人足 expressly adds sufficiency for every person to household provision; the current English omits that second proposition.

additionalCorrections.before: Because high agricultural officers are chosen and encouragement enforced, each man tends a full hundred mu without borrowing oxen;
additionalCorrections.after: Because agricultural officers are carefully selected and every effort is made to encourage and supervise farming, each man tends a full hundred mu of field without needing ox power;
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 高選農官，務盡勸課，人治周田百畝，亦不假牛力；
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 高 modifies 選: officers are carefully selected, not selected for being high-ranking. 勸課 includes encouragement and supervision, and 不假牛力 concerns reliance on ox power, not ownership or a loan of oxen.

additionalCorrections.before: Select agricultural officers with care, strive to the utmost in encouragement and assessment; each man tends a full hundred mu of field and does not borrow ox power;
additionalCorrections.after: Select agricultural officers with care, strive to the utmost in encouragement and assessment; each man tends a full hundred mu of field and does not need ox power;
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 高選農官，務盡勸課，人治周田百畝，亦不假牛力；
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 不假牛力 means not needing or relying on ox power. Restricting it to not borrowing that power leaves open reliance on one’s own oxen, which is not the assertion made here.

additionalCorrections.before: those who labor receive honors and the idle are punished.
additionalCorrections.after: those who labor in the fields receive rewards of public commendation and distinction, while idle farmers are punished by exclusion from standing among their peers.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 力田者受旌顯之賞，惰農者有不齒之罰。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The original drops both the agricultural qualification and the specified 不齒 penalty. The replacement restores the stated commendation and social exclusion without inventing an official rank or a physical banner.

additionalCorrections.before: Offices are matched to need, men do not hold empty posts, and salaries are trimmed to yearly revenue.
additionalCorrections.after: Establish offices according to the work and appoint men according to the offices, so that offices match need and men do not hold empty posts; estimate annual revenue and determine their salaries accordingly.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 又量事置官，量官置人，使官必稱須，人不虛位，度歲入多少，裁而祿之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 量事置官 and 量官置人 state two distinct establishment and staffing rules absent from the summary. 裁而祿之 determines remuneration according to revenue; it does not necessarily prescribe cuts.

additionalCorrections.before: Yet though farming orders issue repeatedly, no magistrate or two-thousand-bushel official works the land with public zeal.
additionalCorrections.after: Yet although orders to promote agriculture are repeatedly issued, none of the two-thousand-bushel administrators or magistrates is intent on diligent public service or keen to make full use of the land’s productive capacity.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 雖務農之令屢發，二千石令長莫有志勤在公、銳盡地利者。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The criticism concerns officials’ diligence in public service and maximizing agricultural productivity, not their personally working the land. Both 志勤在公 and 銳盡地利 must remain explicit.

additionalCorrections.before: Knowing this, Han's founder executed more than ten such officials for false land reports, and under Ming and Zhang the age was nearly peaceful.
additionalCorrections.after: Knowing this, Han's founder summoned and executed two-thousand-bushel officials, numbered in tens, for false reports of reclaimed fields; thus the age of Ming and Zhang was called nearly peaceful.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 故漢祖知其如此，以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數，是以明、章之際，號次升平。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 征殺 includes summoning as well as execution, and 以十數 counts the officials in tens rather than asserting merely more than ten. 漢祖 is retained as supplied without resolving or emending the historical attribution.

additionalCorrections.before: Therefore Han's founder, knowing this, executed more than ten such officials for false reports of reclaimed fields, and in the Ming and Zhang era the age was called nearly peaceful.
additionalCorrections.after: Therefore Han's founder, knowing this, summoned and executed two-thousand-bushel officials, numbered in tens, for false reports of reclaimed fields; thus the age of Ming and Zhang was called nearly peaceful.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 故漢祖知其如此，以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數，是以明、章之際，號次升平。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 征殺 and 以十數 require summoning/execution and a count expressed in tens. This correction does not change 漢祖 or use external chronology to settle its attribution.

additionalCorrections.before: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate and hunger fills the ditches.
additionalCorrections.after: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, with no smoke rising for a thousand li, and people wander and perish from hunger and cold, falling one after another into ditches and gullies.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 自永嘉喪亂，百姓流亡，中原蕭條，千里無煙，饑寒流隕，相繼溝壑。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 千里無煙 is omitted, cold is omitted, and people perishing successively in the gullies are replaced by hunger filling ditches. The replacement restores the people as those suffering and dying.

additionalCorrections.before: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, for a thousand li no smoke rises; hunger and cold flow in ruin and men fall one after another into ditches and gullies.
additionalCorrections.after: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, for a thousand li no smoke rises; people wander and perish from hunger and cold, falling one after another into ditches and gullies.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 自永嘉喪亂，百姓流亡，中原蕭條，千里無煙，饑寒流隕，相繼溝壑。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 饑寒流隕 describes the displaced people wandering and perishing amid hunger and cold. Hunger and cold are not themselves the things that flow in ruin.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Hui, by divine martial strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; land was scarce and four in ten had no fields.
additionalCorrections.after: Murong Hui, by divine martial prowess and sagacious strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign peoples beyond the frontier came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children returning to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; people were numerous, land was scarce, and four in ten had no fields.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 先王以神武聖略，保全一方，威以殄奸，德以懷遠，故九州之人，塞表殊類，繈負萬里，若赤子之歸慈父，流人之多舊土十倍有餘，人殷地狹，故無田者十有四焉。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 塞表 explicitly places the foreign peoples beyond the frontier, and 神武聖略 and 人殷 separately state martial prowess, sagacious strategy, and the numerous population. The existing personal label is retained, not independently established or approved by this English review.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Highness, with heroic endowment, has extended the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li and added a hundred thousand households, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sagacious endowment, has extended the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, expanded the territory by three thousand li and added a hundred thousand households. Your achievement in following in earlier footsteps and extending the enterprise surpasses that of the Earl of the West.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 殿下以英聖之資，克廣先業，南摧強趙，東滅句麗，開境三千，戶增十萬，繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 繼武闡廣 describes following in earlier footsteps and expanding the enterprise; it is not omitted praise or a new martial deed. 有高西伯 asserts surpassing the Earl of the West, not merely rivaling him, and 英聖 includes sagacity.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the merit of martial expansion, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, expanded the territory by three thousand li and increased households by a hundred thousand; your achievement in following in earlier footsteps and extending the enterprise surpasses that of the Earl of the West.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 殿下以英聖之資，克廣先業，南摧強趙，東滅句麗，開境三千，戶增十萬，繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 繼武 is following in footsteps, not continuing martial merit, and 有高西伯 expresses superiority rather than parity. No identity for the predecessor or the Earl is supplied by this correction.

additionalCorrections.before: Reduce the royal parks and settle refugees on the land.
additionalCorrections.after: Reduce and abolish the royal parks to provide the displaced with a livelihood on the land.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 宜省罷諸苑，以業流人。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 省罷 includes abolition as well as reduction; 以業流人 makes provision of a livelihood for the displaced the purpose. This responds directly to the previously described shortage of farmland.

additionalCorrections.before: Even Wei and Jin, though the Way faded, did not reduce the people below seven or eight tenths; official-ox farmers gave six parts to the state and four to the people, private-ox farmers split evenly, and all rejoiced.
additionalCorrections.after: Even Wei and Jin, though theirs was an age when the Way declined, did not exact as much as seven or eight tenths from the people; for those farming with official oxen the state received six parts and the people four, while those using private oxen on official land divided the produce equally with the state. The people were content with this, and everyone rejoiced.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 且魏、晉雖道消之世，猶削百姓不至於七八，持官牛田者官得六分，百姓得四分，私牛而官田者與官中分，百姓安之，人皆悅樂。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 削百姓不至於七八 limits the share exacted from the people, not the share left to them. The six/four and equal divisions confirm the direction. The official ownership of the land in the private-ox arrangement and 百姓安之 are also explicit.

additionalCorrections.before: Even Wei and Jin, though an age of fading Way, still did not reduce the people below seven or eight tenths; those who farmed with official oxen gave six parts to the state and four to the people; those with private oxen on official land split evenly with the state; the people were secure and all rejoiced.
additionalCorrections.after: Even Wei and Jin, though an age of fading Way, still did not exact as much as seven or eight tenths from the people; those who farmed with official oxen gave six parts to the state and four to the people; those with private oxen on official land split evenly with the state; the people were content with this and all rejoiced.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 且魏、晉雖道消之世，猶削百姓不至於七八，持官牛田者官得六分，百姓得四分，私牛而官田者與官中分，百姓安之，人皆悅樂。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 不至於七八 modifies the exaction, so translating it as not reducing the people below seven or eight tenths reverses the shares taken and retained. 安之 refers to the people’s acceptance or contentment with this arrangement.

additionalCorrections.before: With households nearing a hundred thousand crowded against the capital, divide their kindred and move them to western border cities, ruling them with kindness and law so they do not learn the state's strength and weakness.
additionalCorrections.after: With households nearing a hundred thousand crowded against the capital, I fear they will soon become a grave danger to the state. Their brothers and relatives should be divided and moved to the cities on the western frontier, soothed with kindness and restrained by law, so that they cannot scatter among the settled population and learn the state's strength and weakness.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 今戶垂十萬，狹湊都城，恐方將為國家深害，宜分其兄弟宗屬，徙于西境諸城，撫之以恩，檢之以法，使不得散在居人，知國之虛實。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 恐方將為國家深害 is the remonstrator’s explicit fear, not an unqualified editorial fact. The original also omits the restriction on dispersal among resident people, a distinct part of the proposed policy.

additionalCorrections.before: Now households approach a hundred thousand, crowded narrow against the capital; I fear this will soon become a deep harm to the state; it is fitting to divide their brothers and lineage and move them to western border cities, soothe them with kindness and inspect them with law, so they do not scatter among settled people and learn the state's strength and weakness.
additionalCorrections.after: Now households approach a hundred thousand, crowded narrow against the capital; I fear this will soon become a deep harm to the state; it is fitting to divide their brothers and lineage and move them to western border cities, soothe them with kindness and restrain them by law, so they do not scatter among settled people and learn the state's strength and weakness.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 今戶垂十萬，狹湊都城，恐方將為國家深害，宜分其兄弟宗屬，徙于西境諸城，撫之以恩，檢之以法，使不得散在居人，知國之虛實。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 檢之以法 prescribes legal restraint or regulation of these populations, not inspection by means of law. The speaker’s fear and the two restrictions in the closing clause remain unchanged.

additionalCorrections.before: Now the central plain is not yet pacified and stores ought to be enlarged; official posts are numerous and idlers not few; one man who does not plow, the year receives his hunger.
additionalCorrections.after: Now the central plain is not yet pacified and stores ought to be enlarged; official posts are excessively numerous and idlers not few; if one man does not plow, the resulting hunger is suffered that year.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 今中原未平，資畜宜廣，官司猥多，遊食不少，一夫不耕，歲受其饑。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 歲 marks the yearly temporal frame and is not a personified recipient of hunger. 猥多 also states that official posts are excessively, not merely neutrally, numerous.

additionalCorrections.before: Food taken from plowmen feeds idlers; tens of thousands eat without plowing, and the loss is the same; how can every household be provided for and the realm governed to peace!
additionalCorrections.after: Food must be taken from those who plow to feed them; one person consumes the labor of one person, and with tens of thousands living without working, the loss is likewise in the tens of thousands; how can every household be provided for and every person have enough, and government bring about peace!
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 必取於耕者而食之，一人食一人之力，游食數萬，損亦如之，安可以家給人足，治致升平！
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The separate en field omits 一人食一人之力 and 人足 even after the proposed literal repair. The replacement restores the individual labor burden, its aggregate consequence, and both household and personal sufficiency.

additionalCorrections.before: Men of world-ranging talent may be placed as needed.
additionalCorrections.after: Those whose strategic ability is outstanding and whose talent meets the needs of the time may be appointed to posts as required.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 其有經略出世，才稱時求者，自可隨須置之列位。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 經略出世 and 才稱時求 supply distinct qualifications: outstanding strategic ability and talent meeting contemporary needs. The original omits the latter and leaves 列位, appointment to offices, unexpressed.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Highness is broad and clear, thirsting for counsel; men speak even humble truths without hiding.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Highness is sagacious by nature, broad-minded and discerning, thirsting for counsel; therefore people offer all their humble advice, concealing nothing even when it gives offense.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 殿下聖性寬明，思言若渴，故人盡芻蕘，有犯無隱。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 聖性 is explicit praise of the ruler’s nature, and 有犯無隱 says speakers withhold nothing even at the risk of offense. The latter qualification is central to the following defense of punished remonstrators.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Highness is sage in nature, broad and clear, thirsting for words as for water; therefore men exhaust even firewood and grass, offending yet not hiding.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Highness is sage in nature, broad and clear, thirsting for words as for water; therefore people offer all their humble advice, concealing nothing even when it gives offense.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 殿下聖性寬明，思言若渴，故人盡芻蕘，有犯無隱。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 芻蕘 here alludes to counsel from humble people, not the consumption or exhaustion of actual firewood and grass. The context is frank remonstrance, with the risk of offense preserved.

additionalCorrections.before: Officials charged them with demonic speech; Your Highness pardoned their capital crime yet still barred them from court.
additionalCorrections.after: The responsible officials memorialized that their demonic speech offended their superiors and brought them before the law; Your Highness, merciful and broad in acceptance, spared them the death penalty but still demoted and dismissed them, barred them from office, and excluded them from court.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 主者奏以妖言犯上，至之于法，殿下慈弘苞納，恕其大辟，猶削黜禁錮，不齒於朝。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The charge belongs to the responsible officials, not the narrator. 犯上, legal proceedings, the praise 慈弘苞納, and the distinct demotion/dismissal and official disqualification are omitted from the original.

additionalCorrections.before: To punish remonstrating ministers while seeking straight words is like going north to reach Yue!
additionalCorrections.after: To punish remonstrating ministers while seeking straight words is like going north to reach Yue; how could that succeed!
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 罪諫臣而求直言，亦猶北行詣越，豈有得邪！
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 豈有得邪 adds an explicit rhetorical denial that the policy can achieve its aim; the replacement restores that clause without changing the geographic comparison or speaker.

additionalCorrections.before: It is fitting to measure what army and state require, set the number of posts, and return the rest to farming; teach them battle methods; students who after three years have no achievement should also return to farming; they must not vainly fill great posts and block the path of the keen and worthy.
additionalCorrections.after: It is fitting to measure what army and state require, set the number of posts, and return the rest to farming; teach them battle methods; students who after three years have no achievement should also return to farming; they must not merely fill the official complement and block the path of the keen and worthy.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 宜量軍國所須，置其員數，已外歸之于農，教之戰法，學者三年無成，亦宜還之于農，不可徒充大員，以塞聰俊之路。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 員數 and the parallel 速定大員 in s0123 concern the established complement of personnel. 大員 here does not assert that these unaccomplished students occupy especially great or high offices.

additionalCorrections.before: if not, punish me, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
additionalCorrections.after: if not, punish and execute me at once, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 非也，登加罪戮，使天下知朝廷從善如流，罰惡不淹。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The en field separately omits both the immediacy in 登 and the execution in 戮. The first-person object remains Feng Yu, carried over from 臣之所言 in s0301.

additionalCorrections.before: The ruler exists for his people; the people live on grain.
additionalCorrections.after: The ruler takes the people as the foundation of the state; the people depend on grain for life.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 君以黎元為國，黎元以穀為命。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 君以黎元為國 states what constitutes the ruler’s state, not the different proposition that the ruler exists for the people. The parallel dependence on grain is preserved.

additionalCorrections.before: Agriculture is the foundation, yet magistrates ignore spring plowing—those who leave fields idle should face punishment to wake the commanderies.
additionalCorrections.after: Agriculture, then, is the foundation of the state, yet the two-thousand-bushel administrators and magistrates do not obey the orders for the first month of spring or urge on the idle farmers. Those especially negligent in promoting cultivation should be subjected to criminal law, to discipline and spur the subordinate cities.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 然則農者，國之本也，而二千石令長不遵孟春之令，惰農弗勸，宜以尤不修辟者措之刑法，肅厲屬城。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The officials’ failure to encourage idle farmers is explicit and is not simply failure to plow personally. 孟春 is the first month of spring, 尤 marks exceptional negligence, and 屬城 denotes subordinate cities rather than a newly specified tier of commanderies.

additionalCorrections.before: Then farming is the state’s root, yet two-thousand-bushel magistrates and county chiefs do not obey the first month’s orders, lazy farmers are not urged—ought with blame on those who do not cultivate wasteland apply to them criminal law, to awe and encourage dependent cities.
additionalCorrections.after: Then farming is the state’s root, yet two-thousand-bushel administrators and county chiefs do not obey the orders for the first month of spring, and lazy farmers are not urged on; those especially negligent in promoting cultivation should be subjected to criminal law, to awe and spur the dependent cities.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 然則農者，國之本也，而二千石令長不遵孟春之令，惰農弗勸，宜以尤不修辟者措之刑法，肅厲屬城。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 尤 qualifies the especially negligent cases rather than supplying the phrase with blame. 孟春 specifies the first spring month, and 二千石 and 令長 distinguish administrators from the county chiefs under discussion.

additionalCorrections.before: Hunting parks all can be abolished, to give to common people without fields or occupations.
additionalCorrections.after: The hunting parks can all be abolished and their land given to common people without farmland.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 苑囿悉可罷之，以給百姓無田業者。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 田業 is farmland or landed livelihood in this land-distribution instruction, not a disjunction of lacking fields or lacking an occupation. The proposed correction preserves who receives the park land.

additionalCorrections.before: Cap tradesmen and aides to fixed quotas; everyone else goes back to the plow.
additionalCorrections.after: As for the numbers of craftsmen and merchants, the four assistants and the generals shall promptly fix the prescribed complement; the remainder shall return to farming.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 四佐與列將 are the officials charged with setting the complement, not aides whose own numbers are being capped. 百工商賈 includes merchants as well as craftsmen, and 速 requires prompt action.

additionalCorrections.before: Hundred crafts and merchants’ numbers, four assistants and column generals quickly fix great quotas; the rest return to farming.
additionalCorrections.after: As for the numbers of the various craftsmen and merchants, the four assistants and the generals shall quickly fix the prescribed complement; the rest shall return to farming.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 大員 denotes the prescribed complement in this staffing discussion, not quotas that are necessarily great in size. 列將 means the generals collectively and does not establish a category of column generals.

additionalCorrections.before: Strike idle students from the rolls.
additionalCorrections.after: Remove from the rolls students who are unable to undertake the instruction and training.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 學生不任訓教者，亦除員錄。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 不任訓教 specifies inability to undertake instruction or training, not idleness. This is a criterion for removing students from the rolls and should not be replaced by an unsupported moral diagnosis.

additionalCorrections.before: Feng Sheng staunchly upright, deeply attained the body of a royal minister.
additionalCorrections.after: Master Feng is steadfastly upright and deeply embodies the character of a royal minister.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 封生蹇蹇，深得王臣之體。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 生 is a respectful designation attached to Feng, not a supplied personal name Sheng. 王臣之體 concerns the proper character or bearing of a royal minister, not a bodily object acquired by Feng.

additionalCorrections.before: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang led his court within two hundred paces and offered the great sacrifice.
additionalCorrections.after: At the time, one black dragon and one white dragon appeared on Long Mountain. Huang personally led the officials to observe them, remaining more than two hundred paces from the dragons, and offered a sacrifice [the supplied wording 祭乙太宰 is uncertain].
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 去龍二百餘步 means more than two hundred paces away, not within two hundred. 親 and 觀之 specify personal leadership and observation. The anomalous sacrifice clause is explicitly left unresolved rather than silently read as a named great sacrifice.

additionalCorrections.before: At the time there were black dragon and white dragon each one, appeared at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them, two hundred-odd steps from the dragons, sacrificed with the grand boar offering.
additionalCorrections.after: At the time there were a black dragon and a white dragon, one of each, appearing at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the officials to observe them, more than two hundred steps from the dragons, and offered a sacrifice [the supplied wording 祭乙太宰 is uncertain].
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The supplied 祭乙太宰 does not establish a grand boar offering. The intelligible sacrifice action is retained, with the textual difficulty explicit and no conjectural replacement of the Chinese.

additionalCorrections.before: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.
additionalCorrections.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people’s field rent.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 以久旱，丐百姓田租。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: In the sequence of Huang’s administrative actions, 丐百姓田租 is granting remission of the people’s rent, not begging someone else to excuse a payment. The ruler remains the actor.

additionalCorrections.before: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
additionalCorrections.after: He abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The supplied sentence names abolished commanderies but does not call them empty. That unsupported condition is removed while retaining every named commandery and the non-exhaustive 等.

additionalCorrections.before: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
additionalCorrections.after: Later he saw a white hare and galloped after it to shoot it; his horse fell and he was injured, and only then did he relate what he had seen.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 馳射 includes shooting, 馬倒 says the horse fell rather than explicitly that Huang was thrown, and 所見 refers back to his sighting. Calling it an omen substitutes an interpretation for the stated act of recounting what he saw.

additionalCorrections.before: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
additionalCorrections.after: He was carried back to the palace in a litter; he summoned Murong Jun and entrusted him with affairs after his death.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 輦 and 宮 specify a litter and the palace; 引俊 is summoning Jun, and 屬以後事 is entrusting subsequent affairs, not merely giving a briefing limited to succession. The existing personal label is retained without an independent identity ruling.

additionalCorrections.before: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.
additionalCorrections.after: Carried in a litter, he returned to the palace; he summoned Jun and entrusted him with affairs after his death.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 引俊 here brings Jun into the dying ruler’s presence, not leading Jun elsewhere. 屬以後事 specifies entrusting affairs to him, as the surrounding injury and death narrative makes clear.

additionalCorrections.before: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
additionalCorrections.after: When Murong Jun assumed the imperial title in usurpation, he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 俊僭號，追諡文明皇帝。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 僭號 specifies assuming an imperial title judged illegitimate by the source, not merely accession to a throne. The existing personal and relationship labels are retained without adding or independently approving an identity or relationship.

cautions: s0233: The supplied 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。 retains a textual and temporal difficulty. No English fields for this unit are supplied for replacement. Do not silently emend its Chinese, choose a death year, or impose a conjectural temporal reading.
s0131: 祭乙太宰 remains anomalous. The proposed additional English replacements mark the uncertainty; they do not establish a particular sacrificial rite or authorize an emendation to the Chinese.

s0279: 邇者 and the subject/construction of 副 remain uncertain. Neither the temporal recently reading nor a nearby-people reading is independently established here; no conjectural replacement is approved.
s0291: 意在無責 remains uncertain between readings involving not assigning blame and seeking freedom from culpability. Neither existing English choice is independently settled by this review.

牧牛 is left as ox/cattle without adjudicating a specialized draft-versus-herding category. Descriptive record relations/actions are not subject to an invented closed vocabulary; this packet contains only source-English proposals.

All supplied source units and both English fields were reviewed, including the full supplied surrounding blocks and repeated passages. No Chinese emendation, date, identity, relationship, chapter, extraction, or publication approval is granted; supplied hashes identify the review scope rather than validate those matters.
